blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At the intermediate level, accounting stops being a set of reports and becomes a shared language — the way sales, operations, HR, marketing and finance all talk about the same thing, using the same definitions. A "margin" means the same to everyone in the room. "Cost" means exactly one thing. "Revenue" is counted the same way in every department.

When that shared language exists, decisions become faster and arguments smaller. When it does not, every meeting begins with a twenty-minute negotiation about which number is actually correct, and ends without the real decision being made.

A good accountant spends real effort teaching the rest of the business to use the language correctly. It is unglamorous work, but over a year it is worth more than a dozen beautiful reports that nobody reads the same way twice.

items.q: According to the text, what does accounting become at the intermediate level?
items.why: "accounting stops being a set of reports and becomes a shared language".

items.q: What happens when the shared language does NOT exist?
options: Meetings begin with a long negotiation about which number is correct
Every department counts revenue the same way
items.why: "every meeting begins with a twenty-minute negotiation about which number is actually correct".

items.q: How does the text describe the work of teaching the language?
items.why: "It is unglamorous work, but over a year it is worth more than a dozen beautiful reports".

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: A clear glossary can be more useful than a polished report.
Teaching the business the language is worthwhile.
Different departments should each define "margin" in their own way.
items.why: Inferência: o texto defende UMA definição para todos — deixar cada área definir "margin" à sua maneira é exatamente o problema.

items.q: What does "nobody reads the same way twice" suggest about those beautiful reports?
options: They are too long for busy managers
They are read only once a year
They are interpreted differently each time, so they don't build agreement
items.why: Inferência: sem definições comuns, o mesmo relatório é interpretado de formas diferentes — por isso não gera acordo.

blocks.instruction: Ouça James mediando a reunião. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
All right, let's stop for a second. We've been going for twenty minutes, and the truth is we've been arguing about a word, not a number. Sales has calculated the margin one way, ops another, and finance a third. Three spreadsheets, three definitions, one very tired room.

Here is what I've noticed. Nobody in this meeting is actually wrong. Each of you has applied a definition that makes sense inside your own department. The problem is that we've never agreed which one this company uses. So we keep having the same fight, month after month, and we've lost hours to it that we will never get back.

So before we touch the forecast again, I want one thing on the whiteboard: a single definition of margin. What we count as cost, what we count as revenue, and the order we subtract them in. Once we've written that down and everyone has signed off on it, this argument disappears for good.

It isn't glamorous work, I know. But if we settle the language today, every meeting after this one gets shorter.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: According to James, what has the meeting really been arguing about?
items.why: "we've been arguing about a word, not a number".

items.q: How many definitions of margin were being used?
items.why: "Sales has calculated the margin one way, ops another, and finance a third… Three spreadsheets, three definitions".

items.q: What does James want written on the whiteboard before touching the forecast again?
items.why: "I want one thing on the whiteboard: a single definition of margin".

items.q: When James says "nobody in this meeting is actually wrong," what is he implying?
options: Finance made the only correct calculation
The disagreement comes from missing agreement, not from mistakes
The meeting was a waste of everyone's time
The margin should not be calculated at all
items.why: Inferência: cada área aplicou uma definição válida internamente — o que falta é uma definição comum, não competência.

items.q: What is James suggesting about the value of fixing the definition today?
options: It matters only to the finance team
It solves this one argument only
It will make this meeting longer but the reports prettier
It will save time in every future meeting
items.why: Inferência: "if we settle the language today, every meeting after this one gets shorter" — o benefício é recorrente.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Finance and sales finally agreed on a shared language for reporting." A shared language is…
options: a common set of definitions everyone uses
a private code used only by finance
a foreign language course for staff
items.why: Shared language = linguagem compartilhada: as mesmas definições usadas por todos.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "We can't compare the two teams until we agree on one clear ___ of 'cost'."
items.why: Definition = definição: o sentido exato acordado para o termo.

items.q: "The margin looked healthy until we included shipping." A margin is…
options: the difference between revenue and cost, as a share
the total revenue of a period
items.why: Margin = margem: quanto sobra da receita depois de descontar os custos.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Each ___ — sales, ops and HR — sent its own version of the figure."
items.why: Department = departamento: cada área da empresa enviou sua própria versão.

items.q: "Please make sure the discount is counted the same way in every report." Here, to count means to…
options: include and record it in the calculation
items.why: To count (here) = contabilizar: incluir e registrar no cálculo.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões de finanças. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The controller still has to sign off on the new margin definition." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "Once agreed, we'll roll out the new glossary to every department." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva, para toda a empresa.

items.q: "Two managers pushed back on the new definition." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "The team agreed the glossary but never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "Let's get everyone on the same page before we touch the forecast." This means to…
options: make sure everyone shares the same understanding
seat everyone at the same table
items.why: Get on the same page = alinhar o entendimento de todos — exatamente o objetivo de uma linguagem compartilhada.
